## Art sitting 4, fourth go: the girls' corridor with its doors evenly spaced

2 rows, each painted twice: the last corridor with only its door spacing changed; and the same corridor laid out again from words.

Run this in the **local ComfyUI**. Press **Run** once.

Each row is one picture, painted twice: **version A** on top, **version B** under it. You choose between them afterwards.

The **Load Image** boxes on the left should already show their pictures. If one shows an error, click **choose file to upload** and pick the file with the same name from `JJK Game images/ui2/early`.

**Cost:** 4 pictures, about **$0.64** (Nano Banana Pro, about $0.16 a picture, charged to your Comfy account).

You don't need to save anything: the results go to ComfyUI's output folder and Claude picks them up from there.

If it stops with a rate-limit or "high demand" error, wait a minute and press **Run** again: a finished picture is reused, not paid for twice (as long as ComfyUI hasn't been restarted).

widgets_values: This is a background picture for a visual novel. Change one thing in this picture and keep everything else exactly as it is. The doors are unevenly spaced: some stand side by side, touching, and others have a stretch of wall between them. Space them evenly. Each side wall keeps exactly three single wooden doors, all the same size and kind as the nearest door on the left. Along each wall there is the same width of plain plastered wall between one door and the next, and no two doors touch or share a frame; the three doors on the right stand opposite the three on the left, so that the two walls mirror each other. Toward the far end the doors grow smaller and closer together only as distance makes them. Keep the camera, the floor, the ceiling and its lights, the window at the far end, the shoe rack and the plant exactly as they are; there is still no window in either side wall. Add nothing else. No people, no animals, no text. Output a 16:9 picture.

widgets_values: This is a background picture for a visual novel: a new picture of a place in a traditional Japanese mountain school. Picture 1 is this place as it was painted before: keep its camera height, its materials, colours and light, its floor, its ceiling lights, its far window, its shoe rack and its plant, and lay out its doors again. THE PLACE: the upstairs corridor of a dormitory, seen from its near end, looking straight along it to the window at the far end. Each side wall has exactly three single wooden doors, six in all, every one the same: a brown wooden door with one small frosted pane, like the nearest door in picture 1. On each wall the doors are evenly spaced, with the same width of plain cream plastered wall before the first door, between each door and the next, and after the last; no two doors touch or share a frame. The left wall and the right wall mirror each other, each door facing the door opposite. Neither side wall has a window. The far end has one window, with trees and sky beyond. The floor is polished timber boards, clear and open across the whole bottom of the picture. The picture is seen from a standing person's eye height. THE LOOK: a real place you could walk into, drawn as a clean modern anime background. Believable materials (wood grain, glass with soft reflections, stone, plaster, fabric), physically believable light with soft shadows and bounced light, real depth. Clean and well kept: walls are fresh and even, with no stains, cracks, peeling, damp patches or dirt, and there is no dust, litter or fallen leaves on the floor or the ground; everything that belongs to the place is still there. Crisp precise edges, clean clear colour, no film grain, no noise, no canvas texture, no visible brush strokes, no haze or glow washing out detail. Through every window a clear, in-focus view. No people, no animals, no text, no logos. Output a 16:9 picture.
